Title: Register with valid synthetic account
Objective: Confirm a visitor can create a member account.
Preconditions: Visitor is signed out; email is not registered.
Steps:
1. Open registration.
2. Enter a synthetic display name, unique email, and valid password.
3. Submit.
Expected Result: One member account is created, the workspace opens, and the header shows the new member.

Title: Reject duplicate email registration
Objective: Confirm normalized email uniqueness is enforced.
Preconditions: A synthetic member account already exists.
Test Data: Existing email with changed letter case
Steps:
1. Sign out.
2. Open registration.
3. Submit the existing email with different letter case and otherwise valid data.
Expected Result: Registration is rejected with a conflict message and no second account is created.

Title: Sign in with valid credentials
Objective: Confirm a registered user can start an authenticated session.
Preconditions: Synthetic member account exists; user is signed out.
Steps:
1. Open sign-in.
2. Enter valid credentials.
3. Submit.
Expected Result: The workspace opens and identifies the correct display name and role.

Title: Reject incorrect password
Objective: Confirm incorrect credentials do not create a session.
Preconditions: Synthetic member account exists; user is signed out.
Steps:
1. Enter the registered email and an incorrect password.
2. Submit.
Expected Result: Access is denied with a clear credential error and the sign-in page remains displayed.

Title: Reject unknown email
Objective: Confirm an unknown identity receives the same credential error.
Preconditions: User is signed out.
Steps:
1. Enter an unregistered email and valid-format password.
2. Submit.
Expected Result: Access is denied without revealing whether the email exists.

Title: Sign out from workspace
Objective: Confirm sign-out removes the current browser session.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Select Sign out.
2. Attempt to return to the workspace by refreshing the page.
Expected Result: The sign-in page appears and the workspace does not reopen without credentials.

Title: Recover from invalidated session
Objective: Confirm stale local session data does not leave a misleading signed-in state.
Preconditions: Member is signed in; local-only backend can be restarted safely.
Steps:
1. Restart the backend so the local signing key changes.
2. Refresh the workspace.
Expected Result: The stale session is cleared and sign-in is shown with an understandable recovery message.

Title: Update profile name and verify persistence
Objective: Confirm a valid display-name change persists across sessions.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Change the profile display name.
2. Save.
3. Confirm the header changes.
4. Sign out and sign back in.
Expected Result: A success message appears and the updated name remains after the new login.

Title: Reject blank profile name
Objective: Confirm blank display names cannot replace a stored name.
Preconditions: Member is signed in and has a known display name.
Steps:
1. Replace the profile name with spaces.
2. Attempt to save.
Expected Result: Validation rejects the value and the prior name remains stored.

Title: Create task with valid values
Objective: Confirm a member can create and view an owned task.
Preconditions: Member is signed in; target title is unique.
Test Data: Title: Review sprint checklist; Description: Synthetic task
Steps:
1. Enter a valid title and description.
2. Select Add task.
Expected Result: One new active task appears with the submitted values and a creation message.

Title: Reject blank task title
Objective: Confirm a task cannot be created with a blank or whitespace title.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Enter spaces as the title.
2. Enter an optional description.
3. Attempt to submit.
Expected Result: Validation prevents creation and no blank task appears.

Title: Accept task field boundaries
Objective: Confirm maximum allowed title and description lengths are accepted.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Enter values exactly at both maximum lengths.
2. Submit.
Expected Result: The task is created and stored without truncation.

Title: Reject task values over boundaries
Objective: Confirm values above allowed lengths are rejected.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Attempt creation with a title one character over the limit.
2. Repeat with a description one character over the limit.
Expected Result: Each invalid submission is rejected and no overlength value is stored.

Title: Edit owned task
Objective: Confirm valid title and description edits persist.
Preconditions: Member owns an existing task.
Steps:
1. Select Edit on the owned task.
2. Change both fields.
3. Confirm the edit.
4. Refresh the page.
Expected Result: The updated values appear immediately and remain after refresh.

Title: Complete active task
Objective: Confirm an active task can be completed.
Preconditions: Member owns an active task.
Steps:
1. Select Complete.
2. View the Completed filter.
Expected Result: The task is visibly completed, a success message appears, and the task is included under Completed.

Title: Reopen completed task
Objective: Confirm a completed task can return to active state.
Preconditions: Member owns a completed task.
Steps:
1. Select Reopen.
2. View the Active filter.
Expected Result: The task is active, a success message appears, and the task is included under Active.

Title: Cancel task deletion
Objective: Confirm canceling the destructive action preserves the task.
Preconditions: Member owns a task.
Steps:
1. Select Delete.
2. Cancel the confirmation.
3. Refresh the page.
Expected Result: The task remains present and unchanged.

Title: Confirm task deletion
Objective: Confirm an owned task can be deleted after confirmation.
Preconditions: Member owns a disposable synthetic task.
Steps:
1. Select Delete.
2. Confirm the action.
3. Search for the deleted title.
4. Refresh the page.
Expected Result: The task remains absent and a clear deletion message is shown.

Title: Search task title case-insensitively
Objective: Confirm title search returns matching owned tasks regardless of case.
Preconditions: Member owns tasks with distinct titles.
Test Data: Search term using different letter case
Steps:
1. Enter a partial title with different letter case.
2. Review results.
Expected Result: Only owned tasks with matching titles or descriptions appear.

Title: Search task description
Objective: Confirm description text participates in search.
Preconditions: Member owns a task with a unique description term.
Steps: 1. Search for the unique description term.
Expected Result: The matching task appears even when its title does not contain the term.

Title: Show empty state for no matches
Objective: Confirm no-match search is understandable and not treated as an error.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps: 1. Search for a nonexistent term.
Expected Result: No task cards appear and the empty-state message is displayed without an error.

Title: Filter active tasks
Objective: Confirm Active excludes completed tasks.
Preconditions: Member owns at least one active and one completed task.
Steps:
1. Clear search.
2. Select Active.
Expected Result: Every displayed task is active and completed tasks are absent.

Title: Filter completed tasks
Objective: Confirm Completed excludes active tasks.
Preconditions: Member owns at least one active and one completed task.
Steps:
1. Clear search.
2. Select Completed.
Expected Result: Every displayed task is completed and active tasks are absent.

Title: Combine search and status filter
Objective: Confirm every result satisfies both search and status conditions.
Preconditions: Member owns matching active and completed tasks plus nonmatching tasks.
Test Data: Shared search term; Active then Completed
Steps:
1. Enter the shared term.
2. Select Active and record results.
3. Select Completed and record results.
Expected Result: Each result matches the term and the selected state; no task from the opposite state appears.

Title: Display all owned tasks
Objective: Confirm All with no search returns the complete personal list.
Preconditions: Member owns multiple tasks.
Steps:
1. Clear search.
2. Select All.
3. Compare displayed tasks with the known personal list.
Expected Result: Every owned task appears once and no other user task appears.

Title: Administrator views team tasks
Objective: Confirm team oversight includes owner identification for all users.
Preconditions: Administrator and at least two members exist with tasks.
Steps:
1. Sign in as administrator.
2. Select All users tasks.
3. Review owners and records.
Expected Result: Tasks from each user appear with the correct owner name and email.

Title: Other-user tasks are read-only in team view
Objective: Confirm administrator UI does not offer mutations for another user task.
Preconditions: Administrator is in team view and another user owns a task.
Steps:
1. Locate another user task.
2. Inspect available actions.
3. Attempt direct member-route update using the task ID.
Expected Result: No mutation controls appear, the direct request is rejected, and the task remains unchanged.

Title: Member cannot access team oversight
Objective: Confirm team oversight is not available to a member.
Preconditions: Member is signed in.
Steps:
1. Confirm no team-view control is displayed.
2. Request the administrator task endpoint with the member token.
Expected Result: The UI offers no team view and the endpoint returns 403 without team data.

Title: Administrator returns to personal task view
Objective: Confirm the administrator can isolate and manage only their own tasks.
Preconditions: Administrator and another user each own a uniquely named task.
Steps:
1. Sign in as administrator.
2. Select My tasks.
3. Compare the list with known ownership.
4. Edit the administrator-owned task.
Expected Result: Only administrator-owned tasks appear and the administrator can edit their own task.

Title: Members see only their own tasks
Objective: Confirm task-list isolation between two member accounts.
Preconditions: Two members each own uniquely named tasks.
Steps:
1. Sign in as member one and record visible tasks.
2. Sign out.
3. Sign in as member two and record visible tasks.
Expected Result: Each member sees only their own tasks and neither list exposes the other member record.

Title: Complete core workflow with keyboard only
Objective: Confirm critical controls are reachable, operable, ordered, and visibly focused.
Preconditions: Corrected baseline is running; mouse is not used.
Steps:
1. Register or sign in using keyboard only.
2. Create, complete, filter, and delete a task.
3. Update the profile.
4. Sign out.
Expected Result: Every required control is reached in a logical order, activates from the keyboard, and shows visible focus.

Title: Review names, feedback, and page structure
Objective: Confirm controls, messages, headings, and regions expose understandable semantics.
Preconditions: Corrected baseline is running; NVDA is available.
Steps:
1. Review controls and headings with NVDA.
2. Trigger a validation error.
3. Complete a successful action.
4. Record announcements and structure.
Expected Result: Controls have descriptive names, page structure is logical, and new error and success messages are announced.

Title: Measure text and component contrast
Objective: Confirm applicable foreground, background, focus, and component colors meet project targets.
Preconditions: Corrected baseline is running; contrast measurement tool is available.
Test Data: Representative normal, hover, error, success, and focus states
Steps:
1. Identify text and interactive color pairs.
2. Measure normal and focus states.
3. Record ratios and applicable thresholds.
Expected Result: Each applicable pair meets its WCAG 2.2 AA project target or is recorded as a finding.

Title: Review responsive core workflows
Objective: Confirm required content remains usable at narrow and desktop widths.
Preconditions: Current stable Chrome is available.
Steps:
1. At each target width, sign in and review task creation, filters, task actions, profile, and sign-out.
2. Check for clipping and unintended horizontal scrolling.
Expected Result: Content is readable and required controls remain visible and operable at each width.

Title: Refresh valid session without repeating action
Objective: Confirm refresh preserves a valid session and does not repeat the last mutation.
Preconditions: Member has a valid session and just created one uniquely named task.
Steps:
1. Record the task count.
2. Refresh the page.
3. Recheck session, task count, and task state.
Expected Result: The member remains signed in, the task appears once, and no mutation is repeated.

Title: Recover from simulated connection interruption
Objective: Confirm failure and reconnection do not change authorization or falsely report success.
Preconditions: Member is signed in; local backend can be paused safely.
Steps:
1. Pause the local backend.
2. Attempt one task mutation.
3. Record feedback.
4. Restore the backend and sign in if required.
5. Verify task and role state.
Expected Result: No false success is shown; after recovery, authorization is unchanged and the task reflects only confirmed operations.

Title: Review action feedback and destructive clarity
Objective: Confirm common actions communicate outcome and deletion is clearly distinguished.
Preconditions: Member is signed in with a disposable task.
Test Data: Create, update, complete, reopen, cancel delete, confirm delete
Steps:
1. Perform each listed action in sequence.
2. Observe labels, messages, and confirmation wording.
3. Note confusion separately from requirement failures.
Expected Result: Each action has understandable wording and feedback, and deletion requires explicit confirmation.

Title: Verify salted password persistence
Objective: Confirm registration stores a one-way salted hash instead of the submitted password.
Preconditions: A new temporary database is available.
Steps: 1. Register a synthetic member. 2. Query the stored password value. 3. Compare it with the submitted password and another hash of the same password.
Expected Result: The stored value differs from the submitted password, verifies successfully, and differs from a separately generated salted hash.

Title: Reject an unauthenticated protected request
Objective: Confirm protected endpoints return 401 for missing or invalid bearer tokens.
Preconditions: The API is available.
Steps: 1. Request the profile endpoint without a token. 2. Repeat with an invalid token.
Expected Result: Each request returns 401 and no protected data.

Title: Reject update of another member's task
Objective: Confirm a member cannot update a task owned by another member.
Preconditions: Two members and one task owned by member one exist.
Test Data: Member two token; member one task ID
Steps: 1. Record the task row. 2. Submit an update as member two. 3. Inspect the response and stored row.
Expected Result: The API returns 404 and the task row is unchanged.

Title: Reject deletion of another member's task
Objective: Confirm a member cannot delete a task owned by another member.
Preconditions: Two members and one task owned by member one exist.
Test Data: Member two token; member one task ID
Steps: 1. Record the task row count. 2. Submit delete as member two. 3. Inspect the response and stored row.
Expected Result: The API returns 404 and the task row remains present.

Title: Reject unauthenticated task access
Objective: Confirm task endpoints reveal no data when the bearer token is absent or invalid.
Preconditions: At least one task exists.
Steps: 1. Request the task list without a token. 2. Repeat with an invalid token.
Expected Result: Each request returns 401 without task data.

Title: Verify denied mutations leave database unchanged
Objective: Confirm authorization failures do not change another member's task or row counts.
Preconditions: Two members and one task owned by member one exist in a temporary database.
Test Data: Member two token; member one task ID
Steps: 1. Snapshot the task row and count. 2. Attempt update and delete as member two. 3. Query the row and count again.
Expected Result: Values and counts are identical before and after both denied requests.

Title: Validate Must-requirement traceability
Objective: Confirm each Must requirement links to an acceptance criterion and approved test case.
Preconditions: Phase 9 registers are present.
Test Data: Requirements, criteria, cases, and traceability CSV files
Steps: 1. Parse requirement priorities. 2. Resolve acceptance and case links. 3. Report missing or duplicate IDs.
Expected Result: Every Must requirement has a resolvable path and all identifiers are unique.

Title: Apply the smoke quality gate
Objective: Confirm the critical smoke workflow passes before broader release testing.
Preconditions: The corrected baseline and browser are available.
Steps: 1. Run the smoke marker. 2. Review the result and retained report.
Expected Result: All selected smoke tests pass; otherwise broader release testing stops.

Title: Apply the API quality gate
Objective: Confirm critical API contract and authorization coverage has no remaining failure.
Preconditions: The complete API cycle has executed.
Steps: 1. Review planned, passed, failed, and blocked counts. 2. Review critical linked defects.
Expected Result: All 24 API tests pass and no critical contract or authorization defect is open.

Title: Apply the accessibility quality gate
Objective: Confirm accessibility results include manual evidence and no open critical finding.
Preconditions: The Phase 8 assessment and retests are complete.
Test Data: Automated, keyboard, Lighthouse, WAVE, and NVDA evidence
Steps: 1. Review the cycle result. 2. Confirm manual evidence is present. 3. Review open critical findings.
Expected Result: The dedicated suite passes, manual evidence is included, and no critical accessibility finding remains open.

Title: Evaluate the local performance baseline
Objective: Confirm bounded performance observations are compared with NFR-PERF-001.
Preconditions: Phase 10 environment and workload are approved.
Test Data: Local response time, throughput, concurrency, and error-rate observations
Steps: 1. Run the approved local baseline. 2. Compare observations with the target. 3. Record environment and limitations.
Expected Result: The result reports all required measures without presenting local observations as production capacity.

Title: Produce the final release recommendation
Objective: Confirm all planned cycle results, defects, exceptions, and risks support a clear recommendation.
Preconditions: All planned project cycles are complete.
Test Data: Cycle register, execution register, defects, risks, and accepted exceptions
Steps: 1. Reconcile final counts. 2. Review open defects and exceptions. 3. Record technical and stakeholder summaries. 4. State the recommendation.
Expected Result: The final summary is complete, internally consistent, and states Release, Conditional Release, or Do Not Release with reasons.
